The eastern part of the empire, which includes the Lavant, Anatolia, Egypt, and other wealthy regions, engages in frequent wars with the Persian Empire. This wealth and stability allow the Bison Empire to endure for about a thousand years, primarily through trade and diplomacy.

So it became an imperial bureaucracy where warfare was often conducted using mercenaries due to its abundant wealth. The Eastern Empire is quite similar to China in societal organization, despite not being identical.

The Western Empire, much poorer than the East, faces natural barriers like mountains, forests, and rivers, leading to diverse competing societies. The Catholic Church emerges as a dominant power here, increasing in influence as Eastern Europe declines. 

The Catholic Church believes it governs beyond history, deciding who goes to heaven while kings compete for earthly rule. Their power is immense but controversial, as they seek to suppress the divine spark within individuals, leading to conflicts and crusades.

Inquisitors are dispatched to hunt down those who resist their authority, branding heretics and burning them at the stake. As tensions escalate in Western Europe, certain states break away to form Protestantism, a new religion that will be discussed next class.

Constantine makes Christianity the official religion of Rome, unifying ideological differences among churches.
